title: Wire strict-severity gdstrict.toml into check; resolve dual-schema conflict
description: check uses built-in SeverityConfig::strict() and never loads a user's strict-severity profile (preset/[warnings]) from gdstrict.toml, so per-code overrides like INTEGER_DIVISION=off in fixtures/strict_project/gdstrict.toml are silently ignored. Latent design conflict: format side (crates/gdstrict-cli/src/config.rs RawConfig) reads line-length and ignores unknown keys; strict side (crates/gdstrict-strict/src/config.rs parse_config) reads preset/[warnings] and rejects unknown keys like line-length. One gdstrict.toml with both line-length and preset cannot satisfy both parsers; check --config only feeds the format Resolver. Decide on a unified schema, then have check discover+apply the strict severity profile per project. _filed by orchestrator from godot-linter-phase3-strict-6zk.6-cli-check_

title: parse_locator mis-parses file:line:column locators
description: crates/gdstrict-strict/src/lib.rs:140 parse_locator() uses inner.rfind(':') to split path from line. If a locator carries a column suffix like (res://path.gd:42:5), rfind picks the LAST colon: path becomes res://path.gd:42, line becomes 5 (the column). Verified repro: (res://path.gd:42:5) yields (res://path.gd:42, 5) instead of (res://path.gd, 42). Latent under Godot 4.6.2 (file:line only) but corrupts file+line the moment a column appears. Fix: split on first ':' after the res:// scheme, or strip the scheme prefix before scanning. Filed by orchestrator from default-qa QA pass.

title: find_godot never returns None, making test skip path dead
description: crates/gdstrict-strict/src/lib.rs:46 find_godot() returns Some(PathBuf::from(godot)) unconditionally, so it can never return None. The live_strict_extraction test (line 202) doc-comments 'Skipped automatically when no Godot is available' and uses 'let Some(godot) = find_godot() else { skip }' (line 205) -- that else branch is unreachable. The real skip guard is the --version probe (line 210). Misleading for callers relying on None to detect Godot absence. Fix: return None on PATH-lookup failure, or drop the dead Option skip and document the probe as the guard. Filed by orchestrator from default-qa QA pass.

title: render group fits-check ignores trailing same-line content
description: crates/gdstrict-format/src/doc.rs:122 render() Group branch calls fits() with ONLY the group's own doc (&[(ind, Mode::Flat, d)]), not the remaining work-stack content sharing the same line after the group closes. Prettier-style fits() must measure the group plus following content up to the next hard break. Masked today because call() is one outer group with ) inside, but public group()/render() will under-break any nested group followed by more same-line text. Worth fixing before CST->Doc lowering builds nested groups on this engine. Filed by orchestrator from default-qa QA pass.
close_reason: Merged worktree-godot-linter-kw5-render-fits-trailing into main (764ef65). render fits() now measures trailing same-line content (Prettier-correct); +57L doc.rs incl. failing-then-passing test; build+36 tests pass.

title: Strict override.cfg races under concurrent per-file checks of same project
description: gdstrict-strict::check_script (crates/gdstrict-strict/src/lib.rs) injects warning settings via a single override.cfg at the project root, installed/removed per call by the StrictWarnings RAII guard. The Phase 2 concurrent worker pool (godot-linter-phase3-strict-6zk.3) runs many per-file checks against the same project_dir, so concurrent guards race on override.cfg: one call's drop can delete the file another still needs, silently suppressing its warnings. Fix before enabling concurrency: serialize the install (project-level mutex) or isolate each check (per-check project view). Precondition for 6zk.3. _filed by orchestrator from 6zk.1_

title: Spike: tree-sitter-gdscript grammar currency on Godot 4.5
description:
Round-trip a corpus of real Godot 4.5 .gd files through tree-sitter-gdscript and confirm the grammar covers modern syntax.

Cover: typed Dictionary[K,V], Array[T], @annotations, lambdas, await/signal, match patterns, static vars/functions, backslash continuations, multiline strings.

Accept: zero parse errors across the corpus, OR a documented list of grammar gaps with an upstream-fix/vendor-patch plan. This is the single biggest technical risk (PLAN.md section 7.1).

Output: a short findings note + the test corpus committed under fixtures/.

title: Spike: extract strict-mode warnings from Godot headless
description:
Prove that 'godot --headless --check-only --debug --path <project> --script <file.gd>' emits parseable analyzer warnings (UNSAFE_*, UNTYPED_DECLARATION, INFERRED_DECLARATION) on a sample project with deliberately unsafe/untyped code.

Godot docs only promise --check-only parses for errors; warning output is NOT a stable public API. This spike decides whether stderr-parsing is a viable committed path.

Accept: a Rust function that returns structured { file, line, col, code, message } from a known-bad file; per-file latency measured; note the Godot version pinned. Verify behavior with autoload/addon singletons present (known crash risk).

title: Spike: doc-IR formatter prototype with auto-wrapping
description:
Throwaway prototype of the Wadler/Prettier-style document IR (Group, Indent, Line, SoftLine, Text) + width-aware renderer, on one hard wrapping case: a long call chain / argument list that must wrap to one element per line at line-length 100.

Goal: confirm doc-IR over Topiary (auto-wrap needs real layout control). Validate the magic-trailing-comma behavior and idempotency on the case.

Accept: prototype wraps the case correctly and is idempotent (format(format(x)) == format(x)) on it. Decision recorded: doc-IR vs Topiary.

title: gdstrict-strict::find_godot never reports 'not found' (unconditional PATH fallback)
description: crates/gdstrict-strict/src/lib.rs:46-56 — find_godot() returns Some(PathBuf::from("godot")) unconditionally as a PATH fallback, even when no godot is on PATH and never --version probed. Callers relying on it can never honestly detect a missing Godot. gdstrict-cli works around this with its own resolve_godot() (godot.rs) that probes --version and returns typed errors. Have gdstrict-strict reuse the CLI discovery or probe before returning. _filed by orchestrator from 6zk.6-v2_

title: Expose gdstrict_format::format(&str)->String and wire gdstrict-cli to it
description: gdstrict-format has CST->Doc lowering (lower.rs) and a doc renderer (doc.rs) but exposes NO top-level format(source:&str)->String that ties parse->lower->render together. As a result gdstrict-cli (crates/gdstrict-cli/src/format.rs) currently formats via a PLACEHOLDER seam that only normalizes line endings, strips trailing whitespace, and enforces a single trailing newline -- it does not actually reformat (no indentation/wrapping). Fix: add a public format() entry point in gdstrict-format wiring the existing lowering+renderer, then swap it into gdstrict-cli/src/format.rs and strengthen crates/gdstrict-cli/tests/cli.rs to assert real reformatting. This blocks meaningful golden-fixture testing (i7d.6). filed by orchestrator from i7d.5.
close_reason: Resolved by i7d.7: gdstrict_format::format() and format_width(source,width) are public in lib.rs and crates/gdstrict-cli/src/format.rs now calls format_width (real engine, not the whitespace placeholder).
